name: Vyhlídky Diamond Way Buddhist Retreat Center
aka: České Budějovice Diamond Way Buddhist Retreat Center

location.region: České Budějovice Region (South Bohemia), Czech Republic

tradition: Diamond Way Buddhism (Karma Kagyu, lay Tibetan Vajrayana)
technique: Guru yoga and meditation on the 16th Karmapa, phowa and other Diamond Way practices; statue-filling (consecration) courses and study programs are also held on-site
teacherAccess: No resident teacher; visiting Diamond Way lamas and traveling lay teachers lead scheduled weekend courses, study programs and intensive retreats.
retreatOptions: Weekend meditation courses, study programs and statue-filling courses, plus intensive group and individual meditation retreats held regularly at the center.
about: Vyhlídky Diamond Way Buddhist Retreat Center occupies a former farmhouse in the hamlet of Vyhlídky, part of the village of Jivno, about 8km east of České Budějovice in South Bohemia. A group of Buddhist friends bought the building in 1999 and, over years of volunteer labor, money and time, converted it into a meditation retreat center practicing in the Karma Kagyu lineage under Lama Ole Nydahl; both Nydahl and the Nepalese teacher Sherab Gyaltsen Rinpoche have visited. Today the center hosts a wide range of activities, including regular weekend meditation courses, study programs, statue-filling (consecration) courses, and intensive group and individual meditation retreats. As with other Diamond Way centers, there is no resident teacher; visiting lay teachers lead scheduled courses while the property is maintained day-to-day by resident and volunteer practitioners.
schedule: Weekend courses, study programs and intensive meditation retreats scheduled regularly through the year; see the center's program calendar for current dates.
cost: No fees are published on the center's English-language pages; costs for individual courses and retreat stays are announced via the center's program calendar.
foodNotes: Not specified on the center's website.
workNotes: Not specified; as with other Diamond Way centers, day-to-day upkeep is generally handled by resident and volunteer practitioners.
